cash_pct.note: REACH MSNA 2022 AAP: physical cash most preferred. Multiple response, so shares do not sum to 100. Older than 2025 VASyR/MSNA rounds, which were not checked.

vouchers_pct.note: Not reported separately in the MSNA 2022 AAP factsheet.

other_pct.note: Services such as healthcare or education; multiple response.

modality_preference.survey_note: REACH Lebanon MSNA 2022, accountability to affected populations component; sample size not captured. LRP strategy states CVA is the preferred modality of recipients but gives no figure [s4].

mpc.note: Looked in CWG sitrep and LRP CWG strategy; cash is called cost-effective but no ratio is published.

mpc_pct.note: MPCA (recurrent, emergency, seasonal) $300.5M of $1,620.5M LRP appeal. CWG sector appeal is $321.5M (19.8%); Flash Appeal MPCA $134M (20.9% of $639.9M); Addendum $104M.

sectoral_cash_pct.note: All direct CVA other than MPCA ($286.3M), incl. livelihoods cash $115.9M, food cash/vouchers $97.5M, protection $37.8M, rent $26.7M, WASH $8.3M. Computed from CVA overview table.

vouchers_pct.note: Food vouchers are combined with cash for food ($97.5M) in the CVA overview; not separable.

total_cva_pct.note: Direct CVA $586.8M against the $1,620.5M appeal; computed. CVA overview is from the Feb 2026 strategy, before the March escalation.

mpc_pct.note: CWG sector received $136.9M of $750.6M received across LRP, Flash Appeal and Addendum (partner-reported, summed by us; overlap between instruments not ruled out). FTS Flash Appeal only: MPCA $50.9M of $348.6M = 14.6% [s6].

mpc_funded_pct_of_mpc_req.note: Blends LRP, Flash Appeal and Addendum CWG-sector lines (US$136.9M of US$559.5M). LRP-only basis, matching the plan requirements shown: US$32.1M of US$321.5M = 10%. Received $136.9M against $559.5M combined CWG sector appeals (LRP $321.5M + FA $134M + Addendum $104M). By instrument: LRP 10%, FA 42-43%, Addendum 46%. Partners disbursed more than they reported receiving ($100.7M regular + $76.5M FA), so funding is likely under-reported [s5]. FTS: FA MPCA 38% funded [s6].

sectoral_cash_pct.note: Sector funding is reported by sector, not by modality; sectoral cash is not separable.

cbpf_allocations_usd.note: 2026 second reserve allocation only; other 2026 LHF/CERF allocations not found.

mpc_pct.note: Allocation sectors listed are shelter and site management, food security, WASH, health and nutrition, protection; no MPC share stated.

cash_feasibility.note: LRP CWG strategy says market functionality assessments show markets and FSPs can support CVA, but cites no named feasibility study.

cwg.name: Lebanon Cash Working Group (merged with the Basic Assistance sector under LRP 2026)
cwg.evidence_note: Minutes Mar, Jul and Aug 2026 (60+ organisations attending, incl. CashCap and CALP); 2026 strategy and workplan; Q1 and Q3 at-a-glance dashboards; FSP mapping 2026.

ai_summary.headline: Cash is about a third of the LRP, but regular MPCA funding is thin and transfers sit far below the MEB.
ai_summary.narrative: Cash in Lebanon sits across three funding instruments, not one plan. The Lebanon Response Plan (LRP, $1.62bn, 2.99m in need) stays the primary framework [s1]; a Flash Appeal ran March to August ($639.9m) and an LRP Addendum covers September to December ($385.9m) [s2][s3]. Cash Working Group sector requirements are $321.5m (LRP), $134m (Flash Appeal) and $104m (Addendum) [s3]. Planned direct CVA is $586.8m, 36% of the LRP, with MPCA 51% of it [s4]. Partners report only 10% of the LRP cash appeal received, but they disbursed $100.7m in regular and $76.5m in emergency cash, so reporting likely understates delivery [s5]. The Flash Appeal reached 1.66m people, 228% of target, mostly through single instalments [s5]. Displaced Syrian households receive up to $145 a month against an MEB of about $700 for five people [s4][s7]; this appears to be a deliberate trade of depth for coverage. An LRP 2027 cash chapter is in preparation [s8].
barriers: Regular LRP cash only 10% funded on partner reporting (likely under-reported)
Transfers (up to $145 a month) far below the MEB (about $700 for five)
Three overlapping instruments and no LRP in FTS make tracking hard
Social protection coverage limited: AMAN assists about 800,000 Lebanese, roughly half of those in poverty
opportunities: Shock-responsive alignment with MoSA and AMAN, with MoSA as CWG co-lead
Addendum MPCA already 46% funded; common delivery via FSP mapping can lower costs
